Forest-style plot of contrasts over interpretive zones

Source: R/plot-contrasts.R
plot_contrasts.Rd

Draws contrasts (rows) against their estimated difference (x axis) as points with confidence-interval bars and a reference line at the null. A zones layer from geom_es_zones() or geom_mcid_zones(), if given, is drawn first, behind everything else.

Usage

plot_contrasts(x, zones = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
plot_contrasts(
  x,
  zones = NULL,
  ...,
  model = NULL,
  null = 0,
  xlab = "Difference"
)

# S3 method for class 'aov'
plot_contrasts(
  x,
  zones = NULL,
  ...,
  which = NULL,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  xlab = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'TukeyHSD'
plot_contrasts(x, zones = NULL, ..., which = NULL, model = NULL, xlab = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'emmGrid'
plot_contrasts(x, zones = NULL, ..., model = NULL, xlab = NULL)

Arguments

x

An aov fit, a TukeyHSD object, an emmGrid (of means or of contrasts), or a data frame with columns term, estimate, lower, upper.

zones

A zones layer from geom_es_zones() or geom_mcid_zones(), or NULL.

...

Passed to methods. For emmGrid, passed to confint() (e.g. level, adjust).

model

A fitted model (or, for emmeans contrasts, the emmeans grid of means) used to fill a missing sd in zones.

null

Position of the null (reference line). Defaults to 0, or 1 for ratios from emmeans.

xlab

Axis title for the difference axis.

which

For aov and TukeyHSD: the term(s) to plot. Default all; several terms are shown in separate panels.

conf.level

For aov: family-wise confidence level of the Tukey intervals.

Value

A ggplot object.

Which SD converts d to the raw scale

Standardised ("d") thresholds must be multiplied by an SD before they can be drawn over raw differences. plot_contrasts() takes that SD from the fitted model only when the choice is not an extra assumption:

  • One-way, fixed-effects, unweighted linear model (e.g. aov(y ~ group)): the residual SD is the pooled within-group SD, the usual denominator of Cohen's d. It is the same quantity the ANOVA and the Tukey intervals already rely on (equal variances). It is used automatically and a message reports its value.

  • Anything else (several factors, covariates, interactions, weights, GLMs): the residual SD has the variance of every other term removed. That is right for manipulated (randomised) factors and too small for measured factors and covariates, and the model does not record which is which. The function stops and explains the rigorous procedure: (1) decide what SD the benchmark refers to, before seeing results; (2) preferably use an external, pre-specified SD; (3) otherwise refit with only the manipulated factors and use that residual SD (Olejnik & Algina 2003), e.g. sd = pooled_sd(update(model, . ~ treatment)); if every term was manipulated, sd = pooled_sd(model); (4) report the SD's own uncertainty.

Where the model comes from

  • aov fits: pass the fit itself; Tukey contrasts are computed from it.

  • TukeyHSD objects store the call that fitted the model but not the model. When an SD is needed and model is not given, the call is re-evaluated in the calling environment, and the refitted model is used only if its Tukey contrasts reproduce x exactly; otherwise an error asks for model. A message says when this happens.

  • emmGrid of estimated means (from emmeans()): pairwise contrasts are computed (emmeans::contrast(method = "pairwise"), Tukey-adjusted), and the grid's own residual SD is used.

  • emmGrid of contrasts (from contrast() or pairs()): emmeans does not keep the residual SD in contrast grids, so pass the means grid or the fit as model, or set sd.

References

Olejnik S, Algina J (2003). Generalized eta and omega squared statistics: measures of effect size for some common research designs. Psychological Methods 8(4):434-447. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.8.4.434

See also

geom_es_zones(), geom_mcid_zones(), pooled_sd()

Examples

fit <- aov(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth)
plot_contrasts(fit)


# The residual SD of the one-way model converts d to raw differences
plot_contrasts(fit, zones = geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks("cohen_d")))
#> ℹ Converting d thresholds with the residual (pooled within-group) SD of the
#>   one-way model: 0.623.
#>   Set `sd` in the zones layer to use a different SD.


# A TukeyHSD object works too: its model is refitted and checked
tk <- TukeyHSD(fit)
plot_contrasts(tk, zones = geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks("cohen_d")))
#> ℹ Refitted `aov(formula = weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth)` to get the
#>   model's SD; it reproduces these Tukey contrasts exactly.
#> ℹ Converting d thresholds with the residual (pooled within-group) SD of the
#>   one-way model: 0.623.
#>   Set `sd` in the zones layer to use a different SD.


plot_contrasts(fit,
               zones = geom_mcid_zones(mcid_thresholds(lower = -0.3,
                                                       upper = c(0.4, 0.6))))
